$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only · The retirement manifest: what was retired before the release, on 2026-09-23 (CHANGELOG.md, "Retired before the release"). Every identifier is scoped to its registry role: a guard judges a match by file role, never as a substring ban across the repository. The image coordinates exist so a guard can recognise them; nothing here is a pull instruction. The binary embeds this file byte for byte (retirement.go) for the retired-name diagnostics, PDR-E106 and PDR-E107, and the catalog filter reuses it (`podaro.Retirement()`); the retirement guard (hack/retirement_guard.py) reads it.

code.$comment: Files that left with the lab, after what was reusable had been moved out of them (`deliver` from internal/seed/golden.go; `tlsProduct` from internal/runtime/fake_golden.go).

allowed_locations.$comment: Where a retired identifier may still appear, by role — none may hold runnable provisioning content. The retirement guard checks the rule; the list grows only with a reason.
allowed_locations.diagnostics: internal/pdr/pdr.go (PDR-E106, E107, W103 and E215): their codes and explain text; the names they report are read from this manifest, embedded, and never spelled in compiled code — so pdr.go itself needs no allowance
evidence_and_history: CHANGELOG.md (a history note that names what was retired)
protocol_reference: public-docs/USERMANUAL.md §4 (the Authorization scheme the HEC protocol defines and the hec exporter sends)
harness: hack/retirement_allow.txt (its header quotes the search it answers; hack/retirement_scan.py, the binary scan and its self-test, spells nothing)
narrative_name: internal/console/ tests and goldens, internal/api/s9_round12_test.go (the retired playbook's name kept as a vendor-neutral narrative name in test data; test data only)
allowed_locations.$roles_comment: harness and narrative_name are the categories hack/retirement_allow.txt uses beside the roles above: a detector has to spell what it detects, and a narrative name in test data names no product.

in_a_binary.$comment: What a built binary may carry a retired identifier in, in any letter case: the byte-identical embedded copies of the files the listed roles name — the frozen v1alpha1 schemas, which the engine still reads; and `this_manifest`, embedded (retirement.go) for the retired-name diagnostics — and the exact protocol strings below. Every file of a listed role must be embedded as the tree has it (a binary built from another tree fails as such, not as a leak), and each allowed file must carry exactly the names `carries` records, so content appended to a frozen schema fails. hack/retirement_scan.py reads this — the retirement guard imports it — and its self-test proves it.

protocol_strings.reason: the HTTP Event Collector protocol's Authorization scheme, which the hec exporter sends (internal/observe/sinks.go)
